Physical quantity and computation: Overall brightness (exposure): mean luminance across the field of view
Global contrast: standard deviation of luminance across the field of view
Local contrast and fine detail: mean standard deviation of luminance within small image blocks
Focus sharpness: mean squared Sobel gradient of luminance (Tenengrad); sensor noise also raises it
Under-exposure: share of pixels with very low luminance
Over-exposure: share of pixels with any color channel at or near full scale
Glare: share of pixels that are bright and color-poor relative to the frame's own brightness and color
Haze, smoke or turbidity: mean dark-channel value (darkest color channel in small patches)
Blood absorption proxy: mean red fraction of total color, red / (red + green + blue)
Uneven illumination: slope of luminance against distance from the field-of-view center (negative = darker toward the rim)
Tonal range: Shannon entropy of the luminance histogram
